high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of June 29: Market Rate Ceiling Holds at 7.3% for 12-Month Tenors
high.summary: As of June 29, Vietnamese bank deposit rates showed no major adjustments heading into end-of-month, suggesting a period of stabilization in the funding cost environment. The market ceiling for 12-month online deposits remains at **7.3% per annum**, held exclusively by ACB — the only institution currently posting above 7.2% at this tenor. ACB also offers 7.1% for 6-month and 7.2% for 9-month deposits. Saigonbank is the second-highest at 7.2% for 12 months. Notably, six banks now post rates at or above the **7.0% threshold** for 12-month online deposits (MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, VIB, Saigonbank, ACB), while the large state-owned commercial banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) hold steady at **6.8% per annum**.

high.title: VPBank Signs Its First Sustainability-Linked Syndicated Loan Worth USD 1.44 Billion
high.summary:
On June 30, 2026, VPBank formally signed a 3-year sustainability-linked syndicated loan (SLL) with 15 major international financial institutions, with the facility upsized from an initial USD 1.2 billion to USD 1.44 billion (approximately VND 37,900 billion). The signing ceremony was held at VPBank's Hanoi headquarters and attended by the bank's Chairman, CEO, and senior leadership. The loan is structured around Sustainability Performance Targets (SPTs), with interest rate conditions tied to VPBank's annual progress on expanding green and social credit portfolios. The upsizing from 15 international lenders signals robust foreign appetite for Vietnamese banking credit at scale, which carries meaningful FX implications — this inflow of USD 1.44 billion represents a notable source of hard currency supply into Vietnam's financial system and could provide modest near-term support for VND liquidity. For bond investors, this deal may reduce VPBank's need to tap the domestic bond market in the near term, while the ESG-linked structure could attract further international capital. Watch for the disbursement timeline as it will affect USD/VND flows in Q3 2026.

---

high.title: Banking Sector Regulatory Shift: SBV Raises Short-Term Funding Cap for Medium/Long-Term Loans Back to 40%, Revises LDR Calculation
high.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued a new circular reversing a multi-year tightening trend in banking liquidity regulations. The short-term funding for medium/long-term lending ratio (SFL) ceiling has been raised from 30% back to 40% — unwinding the progressive tightening implemented between 2019 and 2023 under Circulars 22/2019 and 08/2020, which had progressively reduced the cap from 40% to 30%. This signals a clear policy pivot toward supporting credit expansion and longer-duration investment financing. Additionally, the new circular modifies the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) calculation by excluding not only demand deposits from the State Treasury but also 80% of State Treasury term deposits from the denominator — effectively loosening LDR constraints for banks with large government budget deposits. **Implications:** This is a structurally bullish signal for Vietnamese bank credit growth, which should support VN-Index bank stocks. For bond markets, accelerated credit growth could reduce banks' appetite for government bonds, potentially pressuring yields upward at the margin. FX traders should monitor whether the credit stimulus triggers inflationary pressure or capital outflows that could weigh on VND. Watch for follow-on SBV communications on credit growth targets.

---

medium.title: Taiwanese Investment Fund Net Sells Vietnamese Equities for 10 Consecutive Quarters
medium.summary:
The Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF — one of the largest foreign ETFs investing in Vietnamese equities, with assets under management of approximately 14.65 billion TWD (~VND 12,000 billion / ~USD 480 million) — has recorded net outflows for 10 consecutive quarters through end of Q2 2026. This marks the longest sustained withdrawal streak since the fund's inception in the Vietnamese market. In Q2 2026 alone, net redemptions totaled approximately 3.28 billion TWD (~VND 2,700 billion / ~USD 108 million). The fund holds a concentrated portfolio of 30 large-cap, high-liquidity Vietnamese stocks representing 99.2% of its assets.

**Relevance for fund managers:** This persistent capital outflow from a major foreign institutional vehicle is a meaningful negative signal for the VN-Index and broader foreign sentiment toward Vietnamese equities. Sustained foreign selling pressure contributes to VND depreciation risk via repatriation of capital (TWD/USD conversion exerting indirect downward pressure on VND). Watch whether other foreign ETFs (e.g., VanEck, VFMVN30 ETF foreign flows) replicate this trend. If outflows accelerate, this could weigh on equity market sentiment and complicate SBV's FX management objectives heading into H2 2026.

medium.title: Advice for Investors Who Bought Gold at Peak Price of VND 180 Million/Tael
medium.summary:
Gold prices in Vietnam have entered a correction phase following a sharp rally, with the USD maintaining strength and the U.S. Federal Reserve signaling a prolonged higher-rate stance. An industry expert from FIDT notes that 60–70% of gold price movements can currently be explained by USD dynamics, with the traditional inverse relationship between a strong dollar and gold prices still intact. Investors who purchased gold near the VND 180 million/tael peak are facing mark-to-market losses as prices have corrected meaningfully. The article underscores growing central bank gold accumulation globally as a structural driver of gold's monetary role.

**Relevance for fund managers:** The Fed's hawkish signaling reinforces a stronger USD environment, which has direct negative implications for VND stability and SBV's FX reserve management. Elevated domestic gold prices historically correlate with increased USD demand (Vietnamese households buying USD to fund gold imports), creating additional depreciation pressure on VND. Monitor whether SBV intervenes to limit gold price volatility or tighten gold import quotas, as this would signal FX reserve conservation priorities.

medium.title: SBV Governor Pham Duc An Attends the 2026 Bank for International Settlements Annual General Meeting
medium.summary: SBV Governor Pham Duc An led a delegation to the 2026 BIS Annual General Meeting, where the BIS Board approved its Annual Report and financial statements for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026. The BIS 2026 Annual Economic Report flagged a two-phase global backdrop: initial resilience driven by AI investment waves and favorable financial conditions, followed by a significant **energy supply shock in early 2026 triggered by the Strait of Hormuz crisis**. The BIS recommended central banks shift focus from short-term shock resilience toward building long-term sustainable foundations. The Governor's attendance signals Vietnam's engagement with global central banking coordination at a time of elevated external uncertainty. For VND traders, the Hormuz energy shock narrative is directly relevant — Vietnam is a net energy importer and a commodity-price-sensitive economy, meaning energy-driven inflation pressures could complicate SBV's rate-easing path and influence VND reserve management decisions in H2 2026. Watch for any SBV communications referencing the BIS findings in upcoming policy guidance.

medium.title: MB Bank (MBB) to Pay 10% Cash Dividend on July 17, 2026
medium.summary: Military Commercial Bank (MB, ticker: MBB) announced that **July 10, 2026** is the shareholder record date for its 2025 cash dividend, with payment scheduled for **July 17, 2026** at a rate of **10% (VND 1,000 per share)**. This cash tranche is part of a total 2025 profit distribution plan of **25%** approved at MB's April 2026 AGM (combining cash and stock components). A 5% personal income tax withholding will apply. For equity investors, this is a near-term catalyst for MBB share price — the ex-dividend date mechanics may see modest selling pressure post-record date. From a banking sector perspective, MB's capacity to distribute a large cash dividend reflects solid 2025 earnings, reinforcing the broader narrative of Vietnamese bank profitability holding up. For fixed income investors, large dividend outflows from major banks are worth monitoring as they can marginally affect short-term liquidity conditions.

medium.title: H1 2026 Investment Channel Performance: Gold and Silver Underperform — VN-Index Posts Modest 4.2% Gain
medium.summary:
The first half of 2026 closed with notable divergence across asset classes in both global and Vietnamese markets. The VN-Index delivered a modest 4.2% return for H1 2026, only marginally ahead of 6-month bank deposit rates — suggesting Vietnamese equities offered limited risk-adjusted outperformance versus the risk-free rate. Globally, Brent crude led all assets with a +16.6% gain, while US equities also performed strongly. By contrast, gold fell approximately 7% and silver declined 17.1% from their January highs, reversing strong 2025 gains. The article attributes the precious metals selloff to a strengthening US dollar and persistently elevated US Treasury yields, as the Federal Reserve has yet to signal monetary easing. For VND and Vietnamese bond traders, the key takeaway is that the Fed's continued hawkish stance keeps upward pressure on the USD broadly, which historically weighs on VND and complicates SBV's FX management. The narrow spread between VN-Index returns and deposit rates may also dampen domestic equity inflows. Watch for any Fed pivot signals that could relieve USD strength and ease pressure on the VND.

---

medium.title: New SBV Circular 29/2026 Brings Good News for Bank and Finance Company Borrowers
medium.summary: SBV Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha signed Circular 29/2026/TT-NHNN on June 30, 2026, amending Circular 39/2016 governing lending activities of credit institutions and foreign bank branches. Key changes include raising the threshold for "small-value loans" — from VND 200 million to VND 400 million at most credit institutions (and VND 200 million at People's Credit Funds) — reducing compliance burdens for micro-lending. A second notable change alters the priority order for overdue debt recovery, shifting to principal-first before interest collection, which benefits borrowers facing financial stress. These regulatory adjustments reflect the SBV's broader accommodative stance, reinforcing the credit-easing narrative seen in the SFL/LDR circular. For bond and FX investors, the key takeaway is that Vietnamese monetary policy remains firmly in growth-support mode as of mid-2026, which may keep lending rates on a downward trajectory but could also gradually build credit risk in the financial system.

medium.title: Goods and Services Prices Remain Stubbornly High After Fuel Price Decline
medium.summary: Consumer prices for food, beverages, and essential services across Ho Chi Minh City remain elevated despite a meaningful decline in domestic fuel prices following the de-escalation of Middle East conflict. Survey findings indicate that vendors who raised prices in lockstep with the earlier fuel spike — citing higher input and logistics costs — have so far refused to pass through the subsequent fuel cost savings to end consumers. Street food staples such as pho and rice dishes continue to trade 10–20% above pre-conflict levels. This price stickiness is directly relevant to Vietnam's inflation trajectory and, by extension, the State Bank of Vietnam's monetary policy calculus. If core consumer prices remain rigid on the downside, headline CPI could stay elevated longer than the SBV projects, potentially constraining the central bank's room to ease deposit and lending rates. Fund managers should monitor upcoming monthly CPI releases closely: any upside surprise would reinforce a "hold or tighten" bias for the SBV, supporting short-end VND rates and potentially adding mild upward pressure on government bond yields at the shorter end of the curve.

medium.title: The World's Top Rice Import Powerhouse Brings Good News to Vietnam and Thailand
medium.summary: The USDA has revised upward its 2026 rice import forecast for the Philippines to 5.7 million tonnes (up 100,000 tonnes from the prior estimate of 5.6 million tonnes), citing declining domestic production, higher input costs, shrinking cultivated area, and adverse weather risks. The Philippines has already imported approximately 2.42 million tonnes year-to-date as of June 11. This is a modestly positive signal for Vietnam's trade balance, as Vietnam is one of the Philippines' primary rice suppliers. Stronger rice export volumes would support Vietnam's goods export receipts and contribute to a healthier current account position, which in turn provides underlying support for the VND. While the magnitude of this single commodity flow is unlikely to be a primary driver of USD/VND, it is a constructive incremental data point for the current account outlook. Watch for official Vietnamese rice export volume and value data in upcoming trade statistics releases.
